jobs.title: Senior CAD Engineer – Physical Verification
jobs.description:
**Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for** ***all*****.**

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Develop and maintain physical verification tools, flows, and methodologies for DRAM, HBM, NAND, and emerging memory products.
* Develop, debug, qualify, and release Siemens Calibre design rule checking (DRC) and layout versus schematic (LVS) rule decks using Standard Verification Rule Format (SVRF).
* Translate process design rules into verification checks, and define the test cases, coverage criteria, and regression methods that qualify them.
* Partner with process, design, layout, modeling, and verification teams to define signoff strategies and resolve verification issues.
* Guide design teams on verification methodologies, waivers, and debugging, and provide training, documentation, and production support.
* Evaluate EDA technologies that improve verification quality, performance, and capacity.
* Automate verification setup, execution, and reporting, including AI-assisted analysis and debugging.
* Lead technical projects and contribute to the physical verification roadmap.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science, or equivalent.
* 5+ years of industry experience in **CAD, EDA,** or **semiconductor design.**
* Experience with DRC and LVS **physical verification**, IC layout, and process design rules.
* Ability to interpret design-rule requirements and resolve complex verification issues in production flows.
* Proficiency in **Python** and at least one additional language, such as SKILL, Tcl, Perl, C, or C++, plus Linux/Unix and shell scripting.
* **Solid CMOS and VLSI fundamentals**, with clear communication and practical debugging skills across global teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience developing and qualifying Calibre DRC and LVS rule decks in SVRF, using nmDRC, nmLVS, and Results Viewing Environment (RVE).
* Knowledge of layout-dependent effects and electrical rule checking (ERC), programmable ERC (PERC), antenna, and density checks.
* Experience optimizing rule-deck coverage, runtime, and memory use.
* Experience with Cadence Virtuoso, SKILL, or Cadence physical verification tools.
* Experience applying AI/ML, large language models, or agentic AI to engineering workflows.
* Experience with source control, automated testing, and release management.
* Knowledge of DRAM, HBM, NAND, or emerging memory development.

jobs.title: Research Lab Technician II - Data Analysis
jobs.description:
**Job ID** REQ20182581 **Category** Laboratory

  

The USC Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, Titus Family Department of Clinical Pharmacy, is seeking a Research Lab Technician II to support ongoing studies in immunogenomics, cancer genomics and therapeutics.

  
  

We are a translational genomics and experimental therapeutics lab focused on identifying and investigating novel therapeutic targets in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and developing new therapeutic strategies. We seek a highly motivated, detail-oriented individual to perform molecular, cellular, and in vivo experiments and support the day-to-day operation of the laboratory.

  
  

**Responsibilities**

  
  

* Process and run quality control on next-generation sequencing data (e.g., RNA-seq, whole-exome/genome sequencing, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, single-cell sequencing) using established pipelines
* Perform downstream analyses, including differential expression, variant calling and annotation, pathway enrichment, and clustering, under the guidance of the Principal Investigator and senior lab members
* Analyze data from high-throughput drug screens, flow cytometry, and preclinical mouse studies; perform basic statistical analyses
* Mine public ‘omics’ resources (e.g., TCGA, BeatAML, GEO, DepMap) to support target discovery and validation
* Maintain, document, and update analysis pipelines and scripts using version control
* Organize and manage lab datasets, sample metadata, and clinical annotations in compliance with IRB and data security requirements
* Run jobs on USC’s high-performance computing cluster and manage data storage
* Prepare figures, tables, and summaries of results for lab meetings, presentations, and manuscripts
  

  

**Minimum Preferred Qualifications**

  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, or a related field
* Hands-on laboratory experience with routine molecular biology and cell culture techniques
* Excellent organizational, record-keeping, and communication skills
* Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

  
  

* Master’s degree or 1–2 years of research laboratory experience
* Experience with flow cytometry, NGS sample preparation, or high-throughput assays
* Experience with mouse handling and in vivo studies
* Familiarity with basic data analysis tools (e.g., R, Python, GraphPad Prism) or interest in learning bioinformatics
* Background in cancer biology or hematologic malignancies
  

  

**Applicants should attach the following:**

  
  

* Cover letter describing research experience and interests
* Résumé or CV
* Names and contact information for two to three references
  

  

The hourly rate range for this position is $25.71 - $28.32. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.

  
  
Minimum Education: Associate's degree, Specialized/technical training, Combined experience/education as substitute for minimum education Minimum Experience: 2 years Minimum Field of Expertise: Working knowledge of laboratory equipment and research protocols. Knowledge of computer analysis techniques and ability to provide routine analysis and interpretation of research data.

**Job ID** REQ20182581 **Posted Date** 10/31/2026

jobs.title: Sr. Research Associate, Molecular Biology
jobs.description:
The Senior Research Associate independently executes complex research and development activities supporting the development and characterization of the company’s cell therapy programs. Working with minimal supervision, this role performs and optimizes translational and molecular biology workflows, analyzes and interprets experimental data, troubleshoots technical challenges, and contributes to experimental planning and method development. The position collaborates with R&D and cross-functional teams and serves as a technical resource in support of project and research objectives.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Independently execute and optimize single cell and single nucleus RNA sequencing workflows, including cell thawing and counting, sample preparation, library preparation, library quality control, and preparation of libraries for sequencing.
* Execute molecular biology and biomarker assay workflows including nucleic acid isolation, PCR, qPCR, sequencing related assays, and sample preparation and processing for LC-MS based analyses.
* Support cell culture workflows and perform other research and development activities in collaboration with R&D scientists and cross-functional partners.
* Make detailed observations; compile, analyze, and interpret experimental and sequencing data; assess data quality; summarize conclusions; and communicate findings to supervisors and the broader R&D team.
* Independently troubleshoot technical issues involving experimental design, assay execution, sequencing workflows, instrumentation, and data quality; recommend and implement solutions within established project objectives.
* Contribute to experimental planning, assay optimization, quality-control strategy, and method development to meet evolving project and translational research needs.
* Evaluate, develop, optimize, and implement new methods, assays, and technologies to advance assigned projects and platform capabilities.
* Independently maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready laboratory notebooks, experimental records, protocols, and data documentation in accordance with applicable quality and documentation requirements.
* Prepare figures, data summaries, protocols, technical reports, and other documentation for internal reviews, project discussions, and knowledge sharing.
* Maintain laboratory organization and the readiness of equipment, reagents, consumables, and general laboratory supplies.
* Serve as a technical resource within areas of expertise and support training, knowledge sharing, and laboratory best practices.
* Maintain current knowledge of relevant scientific literature, translational research methods, sequencing technologies, biomarker applications, and emerging industry practices while complying with applicable safety, training, and quality requirements.
* May participate in scientific conferences and contribute to scientific publications, internal presentations, or other scientific communications, as appropriate.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in biology, biochemistry or related disciplines is required.
* A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in molecular biology or a related laboratory setting is preferred; or equivalent and relevant combination of education and experience.
* Hands-on experience with next-generation sequencing workflows, including sample preparation, library preparation, library quality control, and sequencing-readiness activities.
* Experience with single-cell or single-nucleus RNA sequencing is strongly preferred.
* Experience with molecular biology and translational assay workflows, including nucleic acid isolation, PCR/qPCR, biomarker analysis, biological sample processing, and preparation for downstream analyses. Experience with LC-MS sample preparation is preferred.

**JOB SPECIFICATIONS:**

* **Technical Proficiency:** Strong molecular and cell biology laboratory skills and a solid understanding of scientific principles, with the ability to independently execute and optimize workflows.
* **Analytical Skills:** Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess data quality, interpret experimental results, troubleshoot technical issues, and draw appropriate conclusions.
* **Data Analysis & Presentation:** Ability to efficiently organize, analyze, interpret, and present experimental and sequencing data to scientific and cross-functional audiences.
* **Communication Skills:** Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly document procedures and results, communicate scientific findings, and collaborate effectively across teams.
* **Organization & Documentation:** Excellent organizational skills with demonstrated ability to maintain thorough, accurate experimental records, laboratory notebooks, protocols, and supporting documentation.
* **Collaboration & Adaptability:** Ability to work effectively in cross-functional and team-based environments, adapt to changing project priorities, and share technical knowledge and best practices with colleagues.
* **Professional Scientific Expertise:** Maintains current knowledge of relevant scientific literature, technologies, and industry best practices while complying with applicable safety, training, and quality requirements.
* **Technology & Computational Skills:** Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and familiarity with data analysis tools or programming languages such as R, Python, or Bash.
* **Flexibility:** Willingness to work flexible hours, including occasional weekends, as needed to support experiments, sample processing, sequencing runs, or project timelines.

jobs.title: Staff Research Associate, Linguistics (9613C) #89726
jobs.description:
Staff Research Associate, Linguistics (9613C) #89726 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Linguistics, within the Social Sciences Division of the College of Letters and Science, is highly regarded in the linguistics community. Our faculty and students have close contacts with other departments and programs on campus, including Anthropology, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, Education, Native American Studies, Philosophy, Psychology, and many language and literature departments. We are home to several laboratories and a language archive. The department consists of 25 faculty members, including emeritae, approximately 35 graduate students, and 100+ undergraduate majors. We also host postdocs, visiting scholars, researchers, and 6 staff FTE.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Staff Research Associate supports the UC Berkeley site of a multi-site, NIH-funded research project (R01DC021849; lead site: Northwestern University) examining pragmatic language and social communication in autism across two typologically distinct languages, English and Mandarin Chinese. The Berkeley site, directed by the Principal Investigator (Prof. Alan Yu, Department of Linguistics), is responsible for enrolling and testing Mandarin-speaking participants.
  
  
Under close technical supervision by the PI and the postdoctoral researcher, the position exists to carry out participant recruitment and data collection with Mandarin-speaking autistic individuals, their family members, and non-autistic comparison participants, and to ensure that all assessments, language samples, and neurophysiological (EEG) data collected at Berkeley are obtained, managed, and transferred according to the shared multi-site protocol so that they can be combined with data collected at Northwestern University.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
The First Review Date for this job is November 13, 2026. For full consideration, please apply by the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
Participant Testing and Data Collection - 50%
  
  
Under close technical supervision and following established procedures, administers the study's standardized testing battery, primarily in Mandarin and in English where required, to autistic individuals, their family members, and non-autistic comparison participants, including minors. The battery includes clinical-behavioral characterization measures, cognitive IQ and standardized language tests, narrative and conversational language elicitation tasks, electroencephalography EEG experiments, and questionnaires.
  
Obtains informed consent and assent; prepares testing rooms, materials, and equipment; fits EEG caps and electrodes, monitors signal quality, and runs computerized experiments; audio- and video-records sessions; and scores assessments according to test manuals and study protocol after training to study standards.
  
**End Result:** Complete, valid, protocol-consistent data from every session that are comparable with data collected at the lead site, and a safe, respectful, and well-paced experience for each participant and family.
  
  
Recruitment, Screening, and Scheduling - 25%
  
  
Conducts outreach to Mandarin-speaking families through community organizations, autism service providers, parent networks, and occasional community events; responds to inquiries; and conducts eligibility screening by phone or online in Mandarin and English.
  
Schedules research visits, including visits involving multiple members of the same family; sends reminders and visit instructions; and maintains an accurate recruitment and enrollment tracking log.
  
**End Result:** Steady enrollment that meets site recruitment targets, with accurate and up-to-date records of participant contact, eligibility, and visit status.
  
  
Data Management and Quality Control - 15%
  
  
Enters and verifies assessment and questionnaire data in secure study databases; organizes, labels, and de-identifies audio, video, and EEG files; performs initial quality checks on collected data; and transfers data to the lead site through approved secure platforms.
  
**End Result:** An accurate, secure, and analysis-ready Berkeley site dataset that is fully aligned with the multi-site data structure.
  
  
Regulatory Compliance and Project Coordination - 10%
  
  
Maintains IRB documentation, consent records, and protocol training logs; documents and reports protocol deviations to the PI; attends regular meetings with the Northwestern research team; prepares progress summaries for the PI; and maintains testing equipment and supply inventory.

new_jobs.title: Research Lab Technician II - Data Analysis
new_jobs.description:
**Job ID** REQ20182581 **Category** Laboratory

  

The USC Alfred E. Mann School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, Titus Family Department of Clinical Pharmacy, is seeking a Research Lab Technician II to support ongoing studies in immunogenomics, cancer genomics and therapeutics.

  
  

We are a translational genomics and experimental therapeutics lab focused on identifying and investigating novel therapeutic targets in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and developing new therapeutic strategies. We seek a highly motivated, detail-oriented individual to perform molecular, cellular, and in vivo experiments and support the day-to-day operation of the laboratory.

  
  

**Responsibilities**

  
  

* Process and run quality control on next-generation sequencing data (e.g., RNA-seq, whole-exome/genome sequencing, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, single-cell sequencing) using established pipelines
* Perform downstream analyses, including differential expression, variant calling and annotation, pathway enrichment, and clustering, under the guidance of the Principal Investigator and senior lab members
* Analyze data from high-throughput drug screens, flow cytometry, and preclinical mouse studies; perform basic statistical analyses
* Mine public ‘omics’ resources (e.g., TCGA, BeatAML, GEO, DepMap) to support target discovery and validation
* Maintain, document, and update analysis pipelines and scripts using version control
* Organize and manage lab datasets, sample metadata, and clinical annotations in compliance with IRB and data security requirements
* Run jobs on USC’s high-performance computing cluster and manage data storage
* Prepare figures, tables, and summaries of results for lab meetings, presentations, and manuscripts
  

  

**Minimum Preferred Qualifications**

  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, or a related field
* Hands-on laboratory experience with routine molecular biology and cell culture techniques
* Excellent organizational, record-keeping, and communication skills
* Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

  
  

* Master’s degree or 1–2 years of research laboratory experience
* Experience with flow cytometry, NGS sample preparation, or high-throughput assays
* Experience with mouse handling and in vivo studies
* Familiarity with basic data analysis tools (e.g., R, Python, GraphPad Prism) or interest in learning bioinformatics
* Background in cancer biology or hematologic malignancies
  

  

**Applicants should attach the following:**

  
  

* Cover letter describing research experience and interests
* Résumé or CV
* Names and contact information for two to three references
  

  

The hourly rate range for this position is $25.71 - $28.32. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.

  
  
Minimum Education: Associate's degree, Specialized/technical training, Combined experience/education as substitute for minimum education Minimum Experience: 2 years Minimum Field of Expertise: Working knowledge of laboratory equipment and research protocols. Knowledge of computer analysis techniques and ability to provide routine analysis and interpretation of research data.

Staff Research Associate, Linguistics (9613C) #89726 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Linguistics, within the Social Sciences Division of the College of Letters and Science, is highly regarded in the linguistics community. Our faculty and students have close contacts with other departments and programs on campus, including Anthropology, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, Education, Native American Studies, Philosophy, Psychology, and many language and literature departments. We are home to several laboratories and a language archive. The department consists of 25 faculty members, including emeritae, approximately 35 graduate students, and 100+ undergraduate majors. We also host postdocs, visiting scholars, researchers, and 6 staff FTE.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Staff Research Associate supports the UC Berkeley site of a multi-site, NIH-funded research project (R01DC021849; lead site: Northwestern University) examining pragmatic language and social communication in autism across two typologically distinct languages, English and Mandarin Chinese. The Berkeley site, directed by the Principal Investigator (Prof. Alan Yu, Department of Linguistics), is responsible for enrolling and testing Mandarin-speaking participants.
  
  
Under close technical supervision by the PI and the postdoctoral researcher, the position exists to carry out participant recruitment and data collection with Mandarin-speaking autistic individuals, their family members, and non-autistic comparison participants, and to ensure that all assessments, language samples, and neurophysiological (EEG) data collected at Berkeley are obtained, managed, and transferred according to the shared multi-site protocol so that they can be combined with data collected at Northwestern University.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
The First Review Date for this job is November 13, 2026. For full consideration, please apply by the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
Participant Testing and Data Collection - 50%
  
  
Under close technical supervision and following established procedures, administers the study's standardized testing battery, primarily in Mandarin and in English where required, to autistic individuals, their family members, and non-autistic comparison participants, including minors. The battery includes clinical-behavioral characterization measures, cognitive IQ and standardized language tests, narrative and conversational language elicitation tasks, electroencephalography EEG experiments, and questionnaires.
  
Obtains informed consent and assent; prepares testing rooms, materials, and equipment; fits EEG caps and electrodes, monitors signal quality, and runs computerized experiments; audio- and video-records sessions; and scores assessments according to test manuals and study protocol after training to study standards.
  
**End Result:** Complete, valid, protocol-consistent data from every session that are comparable with data collected at the lead site, and a safe, respectful, and well-paced experience for each participant and family.
  
  
Recruitment, Screening, and Scheduling - 25%
  
  
Conducts outreach to Mandarin-speaking families through community organizations, autism service providers, parent networks, and occasional community events; responds to inquiries; and conducts eligibility screening by phone or online in Mandarin and English.
  
Schedules research visits, including visits involving multiple members of the same family; sends reminders and visit instructions; and maintains an accurate recruitment and enrollment tracking log.
  
**End Result:** Steady enrollment that meets site recruitment targets, with accurate and up-to-date records of participant contact, eligibility, and visit status.
  
  
Data Management and Quality Control - 15%
  
  
Enters and verifies assessment and questionnaire data in secure study databases; organizes, labels, and de-identifies audio, video, and EEG files; performs initial quality checks on collected data; and transfers data to the lead site through approved secure platforms.
  
**End Result:** An accurate, secure, and analysis-ready Berkeley site dataset that is fully aligned with the multi-site data structure.
  
  
Regulatory Compliance and Project Coordination - 10%
  
  
Maintains IRB documentation, consent records, and protocol training logs; documents and reports protocol deviations to the PI; attends regular meetings with the Northwestern research team; prepares progress summaries for the PI; and maintains testing equipment and supply inventory.
  
**End result:** Site operations that remain in compliance with IRB-approved procedures and University policy and stay closely aligned with lead-site procedures and timelines.
